audit.whatIsWrong: content.early tells the reader 'Don't waste Rebuttal on his Q (it's not a projectile worth eating)'. Seismic Shard carries the projectile flag - 'can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects'. So does Unstoppable Force. Malphite throws two of the four things Rebuttal is built to answer.
audit.why: This is a direct instruction to discard the correct play. Rebuttal reflects projectiles, and the entry singles out the one recurring projectile in his kit as the thing NOT to use it on. Everything else in the entry then treats Rebuttal as a generic panic shield.
audit.corrected: Seismic Shard is a projectile and Rebuttal can return it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ground Slam's damage is never explained. Riot: 'Malphite slams the ground, sending out a shockwave that deals magic damage based on his Armor and reduces the Attack Speed of enemies for a short duration.'
audit.why: Two things follow and neither is in the entry. First, his armour purchases are also damage purchases - the item that survives Mel's poke is the same item that raises the damage he returns, so 'he is just getting tankier' is only half the story. Second, the attack-speed cut lands directly on Mel's passive: Searing Brilliance pays out through her next ATTACK, so slowing her attack speed delays the projectile payoff she has been building.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam scales off his own Armor and cuts your attack speed, which is also your Searing Brilliance payoff.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry contradicts itself about armour. early opens 'Malphite stacks armor, not magic resist, so your Radiant Volley poke and empowered autos hurt him far more' - correct, Mel is AP. Then spikes[2] says 'Once Malphite buys armor and a tank item your Q poke chips less', whys[3] says 'buys early armor ... your poke chips a tankier target for less', whys[5] says 'A first armor item ... lets him walk through your poke', and mid says 'Levels 4-5 he's already itemizing armor, so your trades go even-to-his-favor'.
audit.why: Armour reduces physical damage. Mel deals magic damage. Four separate strings credit his armour with blunting poke it cannot touch, after the entry itself established the opposite in its opening line. The reader is told to fear the wrong item timing, and to stop poking exactly when poking is still working.
audit.corrected: Armour does nothing to her magic damage; what his armour actually does is feed Ground Slam.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (E Ground Slam: 'magic damage based on his Armor')

audit.whatIsWrong: Granite Shield's recharge condition is never stated. Riot: 'Malphite is shielded by a layer of rock which absorbs damage up to 10% of his maximum Health. If Malphite has not been hit for a few seconds, this effect recharges.'
audit.why: It is the clearest tempo lever a poke mage has in this lane and it is free. Steady chip keeps the shield permanently down; intermittent poke lets it refill between casts and wastes most of the damage. For a champion whose entire plan is repeated Radiant Volley, 'keep hitting him' versus 'poke and back off' is the difference between the shield being a non-factor and it eating 10% of his max health over and over.
audit.corrected: Granite Shield only recharges after a few seconds without being hit - keep chip on him and it never comes back.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seismic Shard is described only as a slow - 'Q slow', 'his Q slow', 'never sit in his Q slow'. Riot: 'dealing damage upon impact and stealing Move Speed for 3 seconds.' It is a steal, not a slow.
audit.why: A slow means he closes at his own speed while you crawl. A steal means the gap shuts from both ends at once - he is faster by exactly what you lost. For an immobile mage whose only escape plan is walking, that is a materially worse situation than the text describes, and it is why kiting away after eating Q fails more often than readers expect.
audit.corrected: Seismic Shard steals your move speed for 3 seconds rather than merely slowing you.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this matchup with 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' and it is accurate - breakdown.cooldowns contained no numbers and neither layer gave a single cooldown. sequencingCues was 0, the only zero in my slice.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100. At rank 1 that is the longest cooldown in the lane by a wide margin, and it is the entire matchup: surviving or baiting one ult buys more than two minutes of free lane against a champion who cannot otherwise reach a 550-range mage. Without the number the reader has no way to know how big the reward is. Seismic Shard is 8s flat, Ground Slam 7s flat, Thunderclap 10s to 8s.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns in breakdown.cooldowns, the 130s figure carried into the loading line and All-In Windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree about the entire back half of the lane. content.win gives Malphite levels 4-5 through 2+ items; full.phases gives Mel all seven stages at 8/10, 8/10, 8/10, 8/10, 8/10, 7/10, 6/10, with diff FAVOURED. The matchup is 66.67% over 24 games.
audit.why: Both cannot be right and they sit in the same page. The content chart in particular hands Malphite Levels 4-5, which is before Unstoppable Force exists - at 4-5 he has no gap-closer and Mel out-ranges him by her whole kit. His real chart flip is level 6, and pre-empting it by two stages tells the reader to stop playing the lane they are winning.
audit.corrected: content.win[3] moved from 'Malphite' to 'Skill' so the flip lands on his actual spike, with whys[3] rewritten to match. Levels 6 onward left with Malphite, which is defensible. The full layer's blanket 8/10 chart is the more wrong of the two but phases[N].side and diffRating are unreachable - see notes.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (R Unstoppable Force is the level-6 spike)

audit.whatIsWrong: report[11] Common Mistakes lists generic template lines and misses every mistake this matchup actually produces.
audit.why: The three real ones are all documented above: holding Rebuttal off Seismic Shard because the entry told you it is not a projectile, letting Granite Shield refill between pokes, and standing in Q while it steals your speed.

edits.before: Track Malphite’s Unstoppable Force: Unstoppable engage — usually banked for teamfights, punish lane passivity. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Ground Slam's magic damage scales off his own Armor, so every armour item he buys to blunt your poke is also a direct upgrade to the damage he returns.

edits.before: - Malphite Unstoppable Force: matchup-defining — Unstoppable engage — usually banked for teamfights, punish lane passivity. Check it before every step-up. - W Rebuttal is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Unstoppable Force: 130s at rank 1 — the longest cooldown in the lane, and surviving one buys you two full minutes. - Seismic Shard 8s, and it steals your move speed rather than merely slowing you. - Ground Slam 7s, cutting your attack speed and your passive payoff.

Bad trade: Burning Rebuttal on chip damage and then standing in Unstoppable Force range — your only defensive layer is gone for twenty seconds.

notes: The packet flagged this one with 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' and sequencingCues 0 - the only zero in my slice - and it was accurate; neither layer contained a single number. Unstoppable Force at 130s rank 1 is now stated in three places because it is the whole lane. The most damaging single line was in content.early: 'Don't waste Rebuttal on his Q (it's not a projectile worth eating)'. Seismic Shard is flagged projectile in the kit, so the entry was specifically instructing the reader away from the correct use of Mel's only defensive cooldown. Also worth a wider look: the armour-blunts-your-poke error appears in four separate strings here even though the entry's own opening line gets it right. Mel is AP; armour does nothing to her. If that confusion is templated it will be wrong in every tank matchup in this file.
